properties.description:
`python3 tools/test_loop_nudge.py` — the `AsksTheGraph` case set (~20 cases inside the file's 79).

THE CASE THIS EXISTS FOR is `test_a_level_never_fires`. Every other case in the set would pass on an implementation that nudged whenever the design carried debt — and that implementation would speak in every session forever, which is the fire-on-correct-work failure `ver:skill-triggers` names and the one BL-23 and BL-42 both name. The delta is the feature; the counts are only how it is computed. reflow2's own design has carried 7 unsurfaced gaps and 60 structural defects for weeks, so a level-keyed nudge is not a hypothetical.

WHAT ELSE IS PINNED, each because getting it wrong is silent rather than loud:
  • No baseline, one reading, a fallen count, a class missing from one side, an unreadable file, no probe at all — every one is silence, not a guess.
  • `structural_defects` is NOT a trigger class. HEAL's count moves on edits nobody made to it, so a delta there would report a session for something it did not do.
  • Every class the probe MEASURES has a sentence the nudge can SAY, asserted as a set equality across two processes that share no module.
  • It never adds a second interruption: `claim_nudge` is one flag for the whole session, so a session already being nudged is not nudged twice.
  • THE HOOK RETURNS IMMEDIATELY. Asserted in wall-clock against a real spawn at a closed port. `loop_status` is 22.6s; if this ever blocks on the probe, the feature has become the thing the async shape was chosen to avoid.
  • A failed probe does not erase the last good reading, and a carried reading keeps its OWN age.
  • The RELEASE WORKFLOW stages `graph_probe.py`. `spawn_probe` is silent when the script is not beside it — correct for an older kit, and indistinguishable from a graph with nothing to say — so a sibling added here and not to the kit would ship a hook whose graph branch never runs and never says why.
properties.findings:
`python3 tools/test_loop_nudge.py` — 80 tests, 0 failures, ~21s, run unpiped with the exit code captured on its own line (`| tail` reports tail's status, and this repo has been burned by that three times).

Beyond the suite, the branch was exercised END TO END against the live shared server, on this session's own real numbers rather than fixtures: a baseline of 7 unsurfaced gaps measured before any design write, `graph_probe.py` run for real (23.3s, stateless MCP over `.reflow2/graph.server.json`), and the hook then emitting

    reflow2: this session ADDED design debt and left it — the graph itself says
    so — measured by loop_status against the live graph 23s ago, not counted
    from your tool calls: open gap(s) nobody has put to the user 7 → 10 (+3) —
    run detect-and-ask.

The three gaps were the ones this session genuinely created. It found its own author.

⭐ AND THEN THE SAME RUN FOUND THE FEATURE'S REAL LIMIT, which no fixture would have. Those three gaps did not survive: wiring SATISFIES / ALLOCATED_TO / VERIFIES closed them, and a CONSUMES edge closed a fourth that had been standing, so the session ENDED at 6 — below where it started. A verdict collected from a mid-session reading can therefore name debt already settled. Not fixable by waiting (that is the 23-second block the design exists to avoid), so the message states the reading's AGE and directs the agent to confirm with `loop_status`. Pinned by `test_it_tells_the_agent_to_confirm_because_the_reading_can_be_stale`.

ONE ASSERTION WAS WRONG ON THE FIRST RUN and the correction is worth keeping: `test_it_never_adds_a_second_nudge_to_an_interrupted_session` asserted that the counting nudge's text does NOT contain "detect-and-ask" — but the generic write nudge already names that skill, so the assertion was testing the other branch's wording rather than which branch spoke. Re-keyed on the graph branch's own words ("not counted from your tool calls"). A test that fails for a reason other than the one it is named for is not evidence.
properties.name: The graph nudge fires on a DELTA and never on a level
